issues.legal_issue: A court cannot use liberty to mention after final judgment to reopen a matter already decided or review its decision.
material_facts: The High Court’s first judgment directed restoration of the property and granted liberty to mention if clarification was needed.
After the owners disputed who was entitled to receive possession, the High Court issued a second judgment directing restoration to the owners.
The Supreme Court considered the second judgment unwarranted insofar as it reopened an issue already decided, but examined the merits itself under Article 136.
issues.conclusion: Liberty to mention permits clarification of a judgment where needed, but does not authorize reopening a finally decided issue or reviewing the judgment; the Supreme Court nevertheless considered the merits in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A judgment is final once pronounced and signed, and liberty to mention does not confer a right to re-agitate the matter or confer review jurisdiction. Review is not an inherent power and must be conferred by law, including under Order 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The Court relied on Patel Narshi Thakershi v. Pradyumansinghji Arjunsinghji, AIR 1970 SC 1273, and State of U.P. v. Brahm Datt Sharma, (1987) 2 SCC 179, on the finality of concluded proceedings and the limits on reopening them through a later application.

rule.if: post_judgment_motion_in_concluded_case and final_judgment_pronounced and (matter_already_decided or fresh_issue_requires_separate_proceeding)

predicates.post_judgment_motion_in_concluded_case: A party sought further action in a proceeding after the court had disposed of it.
predicates.final_judgment_pronounced: The court had pronounced and signed its judgment before the later request was made.
predicates.matter_already_decided: The later request sought further adjudication of an issue the court had already decided.
predicates.fresh_issue_requires_separate_proceeding: The later request concerned a new matter or cause of action arising after the proceeding had ended.

issues.definition: When a party seeks further adjudication after a final judgment in a concluded case, and the request concerns an issue already decided or a fresh issue requiring separate proceedings, the matter cannot be reopened through that request.

issues.legal_issue: A former lessee whose fixed-term lease expires while the property is requisitioned and who is no longer in possession is not entitled to receive possession when the requisition ends merely because possession was originally taken from that lessee.
material_facts: The property had been leased for a fixed term, with no renewal clause, and the lease expired while the property was in the State’s possession under requisition.
The former lessees were dispossessed when the State took possession under the requisition order.
By the time restoration was to occur, the lease had expired and the former lessees were not in possession; the owners disputed their entitlement to receive the property.
The Supreme Court preserved the parties’ rights to pursue other proceedings or enforce any agreement in accordance with law.
issues.conclusion: The former lessees had no subsisting right to receive possession after the lease expired and they had been dispossessed. The appeal was dismissed, leaving the parties’ other rights and contentions unaffected.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 108(q) of the Transfer of Property Act, a lessee must put the lessor into possession when the lease is determined. Under Section 116, holding over requires the lessor’s assent; continued possession without consent is distinct from holding over. R.V. Bhupal Prasad v. State of A.P., (1995) 5 SCC 698, explains the distinction between a tenant holding over and a tenant at sufferance. M.C. Chockalingam v. V. Manickavasagam, (1974) 1 SCC 48, establishes that juridical possession, which is protected against wrongful dispossession, is not necessarily lawful possession. The Court also noted that Section 6 of the expired West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 contemplated inquiry into the person appearing entitled to possession, rather than automatic restoration to the person from whom possession had been taken.

predicates.appeal_concerning_restoration_after_requ: A party appealed a decision about who should receive property after State requisition ended.
predicates.fixed_term_lease_expired_before_restorat: The lessee’s fixed-term lease ended before the property was to be restored.
predicates.former_lessee_was_dispossessed: The former lessee was no longer in possession when restoration was to occur because possession had been taken by the State.
predicates.former_lessee_lacked_lessor_assent_to_co: The lessor had not assented to the former lessee continuing as a tenant after the lease ended.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns restoration after requisition and the fixed-term lease has expired, the former lessee has been dispossessed, and the lessor has not assented to continued tenancy, the former lessee is not entitled to receive the property on restoration.
